message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
For the most up‑to‑date information you can check one of the following:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and you’ll see the current AQI, pollutant breakdown, and forecast. |
| **AQICN** | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles” or use the map. It shows real‑time AQI, historical trends, and health recommendations. |
| **Local news sites** | Many LA news outlets (e.g., LA Times, KABC) publish daily air‑quality updates. |
| **Mobile apps** | Apps like “AirVisual,” “Plume Labs: Air Report,” or the EPA’s own “AirNow” app provide push notifications for AQI changes. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s a good idea to check the AQI at least a few hours before you head out, as conditions can change quickly, especially during wildfire season.
